answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, we deposit a dynamic opportunity-cost bond into a secure vault, which coupled with a zero-knowledge verifiable delay function postpones reward distribution until the dawn of successive epochs. If malicious identity multiplication is executed, subgame-perfect slashing matrices penalize these correlated failures across the karst of simulated network nodes, forcing the expected attack utility to be strictly negative. Consequently, honest protocol execution emerges as a robust Nash equilibrium.
